```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Plotting function
source(here("results", "03-diversity", "helper-functions.R"))

# Given a wide-format dataframe where species names are in the column headers,
# subset the data for a particular set of species
subset_for_comp_species <- function(d, comparison) {
    # decompose comparison into species
    species <- str_split_1(comparison, pattern = "-")
    
    # Subset and convert to long-form
    d |>
        select(
            chromosome,
            window_pos_1,
            window_pos_2,
            contains(comparison),
            starts_with(species)
        ) |>
        filter(!if_any(everything(), is.na)) |>
        pivot_longer(names_to = "species", values_to = "pi", contains("_pi")) |>
        rename(
            fst = glue::glue("avg_wc_fst_{comparison}"),
            dxy = glue::glue("avg_dxy_{comparison}"),
        ) |>
        mutate(
            "comparison" = comparison,
            species = str_remove(species, "_pi"),
            species = factor(species, levels = lvls),
            .before = chromosome
        )
}

plot_div_pi_scatter <- function(
        d,
        stat = NULL,
        blank_x = FALSE,
        blank_y = FALSE,
        alpha = 0.4,
        shp = 1,
        n_breaks = 5,
        pal = NULL
) {
    if (is.null(stat)) {
        stop("Choose 'fst' or 'dxy'")
    }
    
    if (is.null(pal)) {
        stop("Provide palette")
    }
    
    p_scatter <- d |>
        ggplot(aes(x = pi, y = .data[[stat]], colour = species)) +
        geom_point(alpha = alpha, shape = shp, show.legend = FALSE) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
        geom_smooth(
            mapping = aes(colour = species),
            method = 'lm',
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        ggpubr::stat_cor(
            method = "spearman",
            digits = 3,
            label.x.npc = "middle",
            label.y.npc = 0.9,
            p.accuracy = 0.001,
            show.legend = FALSE,
            cor.coef.name = "rho",
            size = 4
        ) +
        scale_x_continuous(
            limits = c(0, 0.01),
            breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = n_breaks),
            labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
        )
    
    if (stat == "fst") {
        p_scatter <- p_scatter +
            scale_y_continuous(
                limits = c(0, 1),
                breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = min(n_breaks, 5)),
                labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
            ) +
            labs(y = bquote(italic(F[ST])))
    } else {
        p_scatter <- p_scatter +
            scale_y_continuous(
                limits = c(0, 0.014),
                breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = n_breaks),
                labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
            ) +
            labs(y = bquote(italic(d[XY])))
    }
    
    p_scatter <- p_scatter +
        labs(
            x = "π"
        ) +
        theme(
            strip.background = element_blank(),
            strip.text = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            panel.background = element_blank(),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 14)
        )
    
    if (blank_x) {
        p_scatter <- p_scatter +
            theme(
                axis.title.x = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
                axis.text.x = element_blank()
            )
    }
    
    if (blank_y) {
        p_scatter <- p_scatter +
            theme(
                axis.title.y = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
                axis.text.y = element_blank()
            )
    }
    
    p_dens <- d |>
        ggplot() +
        geom_density(
            mapping = aes(x = pi, y = after_stat(scaled), colour = species),
            linewidth = 0.8,
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
        scale_x_continuous(
            breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = n_breaks),
            labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(
            limits = c(0, 1),
            breaks = c(0, 1),
            labels = c("0", "1")
        ) +
        labs(x = "π") +
        theme_void()
    
    if (!blank_y) {
        p_dens <- p_dens +
            theme(
                axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12)
            )
    }
    
    list("scatter" = p_scatter, "density" = p_dens)
}

plot_fst_dxy_within <- function(
        d,
        blank_x = FALSE,
        blank_y = FALSE,
        alpha = 0.4,
        shp = 1,
        n_breaks = 5,
        pal = NULL
) {
    p_dxy_fst <- d |>
        ggplot(aes(x = avg_dxy, y = avg_wc_fst)) +
        geom_point(
            alpha = alpha,
            shape = shp,
            colour = "grey80",
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        geom_smooth(
            method = 'lm',
            show.legend = FALSE,
            colour = "black"
        ) +
        ggpubr::stat_cor(
            method = "spearman",
            digits = 3,
            label.x.npc = "middle",
            label.y.npc = 0.9,
            p.accuracy = 0.001,
            show.legend = FALSE,
            cor.coef.name = "rho",
            size = 4
        ) +
        scale_x_continuous(
            limits = c(0, 0.015),
            breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = n_breaks),
            labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(
            limits = c(0, 1),
            breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = min(n_breaks, 5)),
            labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
        ) +
        labs(
            x = bquote(italic(d[XY])),
            y = bquote(italic(F[ST]))
        ) +
        theme(
            strip.background = element_blank(),
            strip.text = element_blank(),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 14)
        )
    
    if (blank_x) {
        p_dxy_fst <- p_dxy_fst +
            theme(
                axis.title.x = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
                axis.text.x = element_blank()
            )
    }
    
    if (blank_y) {
        p_dxy_fst <- p_dxy_fst +
            theme(
                axis.title.y = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
                axis.text.y = element_blank()
            )
    }
    
    return(p_dxy_fst)
}
```

Windowed π, F~ST~ and d~XY~ were calculated using the program Pixy using the
*H. major* aligned sequence data. Briefly, samples were joint genotyped using
`bcftools`, before per-sample filters were applied to each individual sample at
each site:

- Depth $\geq$ 10 and $\leq$ 2x the sample's genome-wide average
- Allelic balance $\geq$ 0.2 and $\leq$ 0.8

Any sites that failed to meet these requirements were set to missing (`./.`).
Each variant site was then filtered on `F_MISSING` $\leq$ 0.2 within each population
and across both populations. I.e. at most one missing individual per-site within
species, and two missing individuals per-site across both species.

I've also identified misassembled regions at the start of chromosome 2 that are likely
chromosome Z. As such, we load the mask file below and remove any windows that overlap
the problematic regions of chromosome 2.

```{r mask-regions-chr2}
gr_mask <- read_csv(
    here("results", "05-v2r", "hifi-coverage", "mask-regions.csv"),
    col_types = cols()
) |>
    select(chrom, start = xmin, end = xmax) |>
    mutate(chrom = as.integer(str_remove(chrom, "chr"))) |>
    GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame()
```

Next we load the divergence statistics. 

```{r load-datasets}
df_fst <- dir_ls(
    path = here("results", "03-diversity", "between"),
    glob = "*100kb_fst.txt"
) |>
    read_tsv(col_types = cols()) |>
    mutate(
        comparison = paste(pop1, pop2, sep = '-'),
        chromosome = as.numeric(str_remove(chromosome, 'chr')),
        chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = 1:15),
        .before = pop1
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(avg_wc_fst)) |>
    arrange(comparison, chromosome, window_pos_1)

df_dxy <- dir_ls(
    path = here("results", "03-diversity", "between"),
    glob = "*100kb_dxy.txt"
) |>
    read_tsv(col_types = cols()) |>
    mutate(
        chromosome = as.numeric(str_remove(chromosome, 'chr')),
        chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = 1:15),
        comparison = paste(pop1, pop2, sep = '-'),
        .before = pop1
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(avg_dxy), no_sites >= 1e4) |>
    arrange(chromosome, window_pos_1)

# Join Dxy and Fst (pairwise div) together.
df_data <- inner_join(df_fst, df_dxy)

df_pi <- dir_ls(
    path = here("results", "03-diversity", "within", "ref-hmaj"),
    glob = "*100kb_pi.txt"
) |>
    read_tsv(col_types = cols()) |>
    filter(!is.na(avg_pi), no_sites > 1e4) |>
    arrange(pop, chromosome, window_pos_1) |>
    mutate(
        chromosome = as.numeric(str_remove(chromosome, 'chr')),
        chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = 1:15)
    )
```

Then we mask the problematic regions (remove them from downstream analyses).
This is accomplished by intersecting the divergence windows against the mask
file and removing any that overlap (even by a base-pair).

```{r filter-on-mask}
## Pairwise data
overlaps <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(
    df_data |>
        rename(start = window_pos_1, end = window_pos_2) |>
        GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE),
    gr_mask
)

df_data$overlaps_mask <- FALSE
df_data$overlaps_mask[S4Vectors::queryHits(overlaps)] <- TRUE
df_data <- df_data |>
    filter(!overlaps_mask) |>
    select(-overlaps_mask)

## Within species
overlaps <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(
    df_pi |>
        rename(start = window_pos_1, end = window_pos_2) |>
        GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE),
    gr_mask
)

df_pi$overlaps_mask <- FALSE
df_pi$overlaps_mask[S4Vectors::queryHits(overlaps)] <- TRUE
df_pi <- df_pi |>
    filter(!overlaps_mask)

df_pi |>
    write_csv(here("results", "03-diversity", "within", "ref-hmaj", "clean-data.csv"), col_names = TRUE)
``` 

Then do some more formatting.

```{r}
df_pi_wide <- df_pi |>
    select(pop, chromosome, window_pos_1, window_pos_2, avg_pi) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = pop, values_from = avg_pi) |>
    rename_with(.cols = dplyr::starts_with("H"), .fn = ~ paste0(., "_pi"))

# Create wide-format data for correlation plots
df_div_stats_wide <- df_data |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = comparison, values_from = starts_with("avg_")) |>
    left_join(df_pi_wide)

# ------------ Reference matched statistics ----------------------
# Reference match pi
df_pi_ref_matched <- dir_ls(
    path = here("results", "03-diversity", "within", "ref-matched"),
    glob = "*100kb_pi.txt"
) |>
    read_tsv(col_types = cols()) |>
    filter(!is.na(avg_pi), no_sites > 1e4) |>
    mutate(
        chromosome = as.numeric(str_remove(chromosome, 'chr')),
        chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = 1:16)
    ) |>
    arrange(pop, chromosome, window_pos_1)

df_pi_ref_matched_gw_avg <- df_pi_ref_matched |>
    summarise(
        avg_pi = sum(count_diffs) / sum(count_comparisons),
        .by = c(pop)
    )

# Genome wide avg. Tajima's D from SFS
sfs_tajD <- read_csv(here("data", "sfs-tajD-genome-avg.csv"))
```

I'll also estimate the genome-wide d~XY~ value here

```{r genome-wide-dxy}
df_data |>
    summarise(dxy = sum(count_diffs) / sum(count_comparisons), .by = comparison)
```

## Correlations of diversity statistics

### Within-species correlations

The code below forms figure 3 in the main text. Essentially correlating the diversity statistics
within each pairwise comparison. 

```{r pair-vs-pi}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150
# HCU-HEL
df_div_hcu_hel <- subset_for_comp_species(
    d = df_div_stats_wide,
    comparison = "HCU-HEL"
)

plot_fst_pi_hcu_hel <- plot_div_pi_scatter(
    df_div_hcu_hel,
    stat = "fst",
    pal = pal_within,
    shp = 1,
    alpha = 0.2,
    blank_x = TRUE
)

plot_dxy_pi_hcu_hel <- plot_div_pi_scatter(
    df_div_hcu_hel,
    stat = "dxy",
    pal = pal_within,
    shp = 1,
    alpha = 0.2,
    n_breaks = 7
)

plot_dxy_fst_hcu_hel <- plot_fst_dxy_within(
    d = df_data |> filter(comparison == "HCU-HEL"),
    n_breaks = 5
)

# HCU-HMA
df_div_hcu_hma <- subset_for_comp_species(
    d = df_div_stats_wide,
    comparison = "HCU-HMA"
)

plot_fst_pi_hcu_hma <- plot_div_pi_scatter(
    df_div_hcu_hma,
    stat = "fst",
    pal = pal_within,
    shp = 1,
    alpha = 0.2,
    blank_x = TRUE,
    blank_y = TRUE
)

plot_dxy_pi_hcu_hma <- plot_div_pi_scatter(
    df_div_hcu_hma,
    stat = "dxy",
    pal = pal_within,
    shp = 1,
    alpha = 0.2,
    blank_y = TRUE
)

plot_dxy_fst_hcu_hma <- plot_fst_dxy_within(
    d = df_data |> filter(comparison == "HCU-HMA"),
    n_breaks = 5,
    blank_y = TRUE
)

# HEL-HMA
df_div_hel_hma <- subset_for_comp_species(
    d = df_div_stats_wide,
    comparison = "HEL-HMA"
)

plot_fst_pi_hel_hma <- plot_div_pi_scatter(
    df_div_hel_hma,
    stat = "fst",
    pal = pal_within,
    shp = 1,
    alpha = 0.2,
    blank_x = TRUE,
    blank_y = TRUE
)

plot_dxy_pi_hel_hma <- plot_div_pi_scatter(
    df_div_hel_hma,
    stat = "dxy",
    pal = pal_within,
    shp = 1,
    alpha = 0.2,
    blank_y = TRUE
)

plot_dxy_fst_hel_hma <- plot_fst_dxy_within(
    d = df_data |> filter(comparison == "HEL-HMA"),
    n_breaks = 5,
    blank_y = TRUE
)

fig3 <- list(
    plot_fst_pi_hcu_hel$density,
    plot_fst_pi_hcu_hma$density,
    plot_fst_pi_hel_hma$density,
    plot_fst_pi_hcu_hel$scatter,
    plot_fst_pi_hcu_hma$scatter,
    plot_fst_pi_hel_hma$scatter,
    plot_dxy_pi_hcu_hel$scatter,
    plot_dxy_pi_hcu_hma$scatter,
    plot_dxy_pi_hel_hma$scatter,
    plot_dxy_fst_hcu_hel,
    plot_dxy_fst_hcu_hma,
    plot_dxy_fst_hel_hma
) |>
    wrap_plots(ncol = 3) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(0.3, 1, 1, 1)) +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
    theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"))

pdf(
    file = here(
        "manuscript",

        "figure-3-div-correlation-within-species.pdf"
    ),

)

ragg::agg_png(

fig3
```

### Supplementary figure

Here we fill each point in the pairwise comparisons with the F~ST~ value. This
will highlight that windows reporting high F~ST~ actually have low nucleotide
diversity, which is artifically inflating the value. Each column represents
a comparison.

```{r high-fst-caused-by-low-pi}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150
supp_pi_dxy_fst_fill_hcu_hel <- df_div_stats_wide |>
    select(
        pop1,
        pop2,
        chromosome,
        window_pos_1,
        `avg_wc_fst_HCU-HEL`,
        `avg_dxy_HCU-HEL`,
        HCU_pi,
        HEL_pi
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(names_to = "species", values_to = "pi", ends_with("_pi")) |>
    mutate(
        species = str_remove(species, "_pi"),
        species = case_when(
            species == "HCU" ~ "H. curtus",
            species == "HEL" ~ "H. elegans"
        )
    ) |>
    filter(pop1 == "HCU" & pop2 == "HEL") |>
    ggplot(aes(x = pi, y = `avg_dxy_HCU-HEL`, colour = `avg_wc_fst_HCU-HEL`)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = 'lm', colour = "black") +
    ggpubr::stat_cor(
        method = "spearman",
        digits = 3,
        label.x.npc = "left",
        label.y.npc = 0.9,
        p.accuracy = 0.001,
        show.legend = FALSE,
        cor.coef.name = "rho",
        size = 5
    ) +
    scale_colour_gradientn(
        colours = c("grey90", "grey80", "grey70", "#f3722c"),
        values = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
        breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
        labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1"),
        limits = c(0, 1)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 7),
        labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5),
        labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
        limits = c(0, 0.01)
    ) +
    labs(
        x = "*\U03C0*",
        y = "*d<sub>XY</sub>*",
        colour = "*F<sub>ST</sub>*",
        tag = "A"
    ) +
    ggh4x::facet_wrap2(vars(species), nrow = 1) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
        strip.text = element_text(size = 16, face = "italic"),
        
        axis.title.x = element_markdown(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_markdown(size = 16),
        
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "italic"),
        
        legend.title = element_markdown(size = 16),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.key.size =  unit(1, "cm")
    )

        HMA_pi
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(names_to = "species", values_to = "pi", ends_with("_pi")) |>
    mutate(
        species = str_remove(species, "_pi"),
        species = case_when(
            species == "HEL" ~ "H. elegans",
            species == "HMA" ~ "H. major"
        )
    ) |>
    filter(pop1 == "HEL" & pop2 == "HMA") |>
    ggplot(aes(x = pi, y = `avg_dxy_HEL-HMA`, colour = `avg_wc_fst_HEL-HMA`)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = 'lm', colour = "black") +
    ggpubr::stat_cor(
        method = "spearman",
        digits = 3,
        label.x.npc = "left",
        label.y.npc = 0.9,
        p.accuracy = 0.001,
        show.legend = FALSE,
        cor.coef.name = "rho",
        size = 5
    ) +
    scale_colour_gradientn(
        colours = c("grey90", "grey80", "grey70", "#f3722c"),
        values = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
        breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
        labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1"),
        limits = c(0, 1)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 7),
        labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5),
        labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
        limits = c(0, 0.01)
    ) +
    labs(
        x = "*\U03C0*",
        y = "*d<sub>XY</sub>*",
        colour = "*F<sub>ST</sub>*",
        tag = "C"
    ) +
    ggh4x::facet_wrap2(vars(species), nrow = 1) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
        strip.text = element_text(size = 16, face = "italic"),
        
        axis.title.x = element_markdown(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_markdown(size = 16),
        
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "italic"),
        
        legend.title = element_markdown(size = 16),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.key.size =  unit(1, "cm")
    )

supp_fig_pi_dxy_fst <- (supp_pi_dxy_fst_fill_hcu_hel /
                            supp_pi_dxy_fst_fill_hcu_hma /
                            supp_pi_dxy_fst_fill_hel_hma) +
```

### Between species pairwise correlations

Here we're going to correlate F~ST~ and d~XY~ between each pair of species
comparisons. This is used to asses if the same genomic windows show similar or
different divergence patterns between pairs of snakes.

```{r between-species-div-stat-corr, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150
comparisons_between <- list(
    c("HCU-HEL", "HCU-HMA"),
    c("HCU-HEL", "HEL-HMA"),
    c("HCU-HMA", "HEL-HMA")
)
plot_scatter_between_fst <- imap(comparisons_between, \(comp, idx) {
    comp1 <- case_when(
        comp[[1]] == "HCU-HEL" ~ "H. curtus - H. elegans",
        comp[[1]] == "HCU-HMA" ~ "H. curtus - H. major",
        comp[[1]] == "HEL-HMA" ~ "H. elegans - H. major"
    )
    
    comp2 <- case_when(
        comp[[2]] == "HCU-HEL" ~ "H. curtus - H. elegans",
        comp[[2]] == "HCU-HMA" ~ "H. curtus - H. major",
        comp[[2]] == "HEL-HMA" ~ "H. elegans - H. major"
    )
    
    # space to left/right top/bottom of figures
    expan <- c(0.01, 0.035)
    
    p <- df_data |>
        filter(comparison %in% comp) |>
        select(comparison, chromosome, window_pos_1, avg_wc_fst) |>
        pivot_wider(names_from = comparison, values_from = avg_wc_fst) |>
        ggplot(
            aes(
                x = .data[[comp[1]]],
                y = .data[[comp[2]]]
            )
        ) +
        scale_x_continuous(
            limits = c(0, 1),
            breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1),
            labels = c("0", "0.5", "1"),
            expand = expansion(mult = expan)
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(
            limits = c(0, 1),
            breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1),
            labels = c("0", "0.5", "1"),
            expand = expansion(mult = expan)
        ) +
        geom_point(colour = 'grey80') +
        geom_smooth(method = 'lm', colour = "black") +
        ggpubr::stat_cor(
            method = "spearman",
            digits = 3,
            label.x.npc = "left",
            label.y.npc = "top",
            p.accuracy = 0.001,
            show.legend = FALSE,
            cor.coef.name = "rho",
            size = 5
        ) +
        labs(
            x = comp1,
            y = comp2
        ) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
            axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "italic"),
            axis.title.x = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            panel.border = element_blank(),
            panel.background = element_blank(),
            axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4)
        )
    p
})

plot_scatter_between_dxy <- imap(comparisons_between, \(comp, idx) {
    comp1 <- case_when(
        comp[[1]] == "HCU-HEL" ~ "H. curtus - H. elegans",
```

## Genome scans

Genome scans are used to identify which regions of the genome show high/low
divergence.

### High/low divergence regions

First, the code below is used to Z-normalise windowed estimates of F~ST~ to enable
better comparison between datasets.

```{r ZFst-transformation}
df_data <- df_data |>
    mutate(
        zfst = as.numeric(scale(avg_wc_fst)),
        .by = comparison
    )
```

Windows where ZF~ST~ is $\geq$ 3 and $\leq$ -3 are classified as high- and
low-divergence windows, respectively.

```{r}
df_data <- df_data |>
    mutate(
        classification = case_when(
            zfst <= -3 ~ 'Low',
            zfst >= 3 ~ 'High',
            .default = 'Background'
        ),
        classification = factor(
            classification,
            levels = c("Background", "High", "Low")
        ),
        highlight = ifelse(as.numeric(chromosome) %% 2 == 0, 'even', 'odd')
    )

df_data |>
    write_csv(here("results", "03-diversity", "between", "clean-data.csv"), col_names = TRUE)

# Summary of background, low- and high-divergence windows
df_high_low_div_count <- df_data |>
    summarise(count = n(), .by = c("comparison", "classification")) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = classification, values_from = count)

# Write high/low windows to CSV
df_data |>
    filter_out(classification == "Background") |>
    write_csv(here("manuscript", "tables", "supplementary", "supp-div-scan-high_low_div_regions.csv"))

df_high_low_div_count |>
    gt::gt(rowname_col = "comparison") |>
    gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "-") |>
    gt::fmt_number(columns = 2, sep_mark = ",", drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE) |>
    gt::cols_align(columns = 2:4, align = "center") |>
    gt::tab_style(
        style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        locations = gt::cells_column_labels(everything())
    ) |>
    gt::as_raw_html()
```

Exploring high- and low-divergence windows by chromosome shows the following
distribution.

```{r}
df_data |>
    summarise(
        count = n(),
        .by = c("comparison", "chromosome", "classification")
    ) |>
    filter(classification != "Background") |>
    pivot_wider(
        names_from = c(comparison, classification),
        values_from = count,
        names_sep = " "
    ) |>
    gt::gt() |>
    gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "-") |>
    gt::tab_spanner(
        label = "HCU-HEL",
        columns = c(`HCU-HEL Low`, `HCU-HEL High`)
    ) |>
    gt::tab_spanner(
        label = "HCU-HMA",
        columns = c(`HCU-HMA Low`, `HCU-HMA High`)
    ) |>
    gt::tab_spanner(
        label = "HEL-HMA",
        columns = c(`HEL-HMA Low`, "HEL-HMA High")
    ) |>
    gt::cols_label(
        `HCU-HEL Low` = "Low",
        `HCU-HEL High` = "High",
        `HCU-HMA Low` = "Low",
        `HCU-HMA High` = "High",
        `HEL-HMA Low` = "Low",
        `HEL-HMA High` = "High"
    ) |>
    gt::cols_align(columns = 2:5, align = "center") |>
    gt::cols_align(columns = 6, align = "left") |>
    gt::as_raw_html()
```

We can see that there are a few high-divergence windows across chromosomes,
however we'll see below that these appear to reside within putative centromeric
regions.

### Distribution across the genome (genome-scan)

Here we plot the divergence statistics across the genome. The tandem repeat (TR) output
from `centrominer` is also visualised here. Overlaying the centrominer results illustrates
if high-divergence windows reside in genuine regions of difference, or simply in/around
regions that are known to have lower recombination rates and higher LD.

```{r load-centrominer}
# TR column is 'tandem repeat'. It shows the length of TR found in the window
# 100kb windows - therefore a 100kb value indicates the whole window is TR.
df_centrominer <- fs::dir_ls(
    path = here('results', '00-other', 'centrominer')
) |>
    read_tsv(
        col_names = c("site", "value", "type"),
        col_types = cols(),
        id = 'chromosome'
    ) |>
    mutate(
        chromosome = sub(
            'hydrophis_major\\.(chr.*).tsv',
            '\\1',
            basename(chromosome)
        ),
    ) |>
    filter(chromosome != "chrZ") |>
    mutate(
        chromosome = as.numeric(str_remove(chromosome, "chr")),
        chromosome = factor(
            chromosome,
            levels = 1:15
        )
    ) |>
    arrange(chromosome, site) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = value) |>
    mutate(
        window_pos_1 = site + 1,
        window_pos_2 = window_pos_1 + 5e4 - 1,
        statistic = "Centromere",
        highlight = ifelse(as.numeric(chromosome) %% 2 == 0, 'even', 'odd'),
        # highlight = ifelse(TR >= 25e3, "outlier", highlight)
    ) |>
    select(statistic, chromosome, window_pos_1, window_pos_2, TR, highlight)
```

```{r genome-scan-high-low-div-ZFst}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150
lvls_between <- c("HCU-HMA", "HCU-HEL", "HEL-HMA")

df_data <- df_data |>
    mutate(
        comp_label = case_when(
            comparison == "HCU-HEL" ~ "H. curtus\n-\nH. elegans",
            comparison == "HCU-HMA" ~ "H. curtus\n-\nH. major",
            comparison == "HEL-HMA" ~ "H. elegans\n-\nH. major"
        ),
        .before = pop1
    )

# Genome scan across macro-chromosomes
plot_genome_scan <- df_data |>
    filter(chromosome %in% 1:6) |>
    ggplot(
        aes(
            x = floor((window_pos_1 + window_pos_2) / 2),
            y = zfst
        )
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = highlight), show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey85", "grey70")) +
    ggnewscale::new_scale_colour() + 
    geom_point(
        data = df_data |>
            filter(classification != "Background", chromosome %in% 1:6),
        mapping = aes(colour = classification)
    ) +
    facet_grid(
        rows = vars(comp_label),
        cols = vars(chromosome),
        scales = "free_x",
        switch = "x",
    ) +
    labs(
        x = "Chromosome",
        y = "*ZF~ST~*",
        tag = "B"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(-6, 4),
        breaks = c(-3, 0, 3),
        labels = c("-3", "0", "3"),
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
    guides(
        colour = guide_legend(
            title = "*ZF~ST~*",
            title.position = "top",
            nrow = 1,
            override.aes = list(size = 5)
        )
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#ef233c", "black"), labels = c("≥ 3", "≤ 3")) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_markdown(size = 16),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.text = element_markdown(size = 12),
        legend.title = element_markdown(size = 12),
        plot.margin = grid::unit(c(0, 0, 0, 0), "mm"),
        strip.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
        strip.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "italic"),
        strip.background.x = element_blank(),
        strip.background.y = ggh4x::element_part_rect(side = "l"),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")
    )

# Centrominer figure
plot_centromeres <- df_centrominer |>
    filter(chromosome %in% 1:6) |>
    ggplot(
        aes(
            x = floor((window_pos_1 + window_pos_2) / 2),
            y = TR
        )
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = highlight), show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey85", "grey70")) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
    # geom_hline(yintercept = 25e3, linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = c(0, 25e3, 50e3, 75e3, 100e3),
        labels = scales::number_format(scale = 1e-3),
        expand = c(0,0),
        limits = c(0, 100e3)
    ) +
    facet_grid(
        cols = vars(chromosome),
        scales = "free_x",
        switch = "x"
    ) +
    labs(
        y = "Tandem repeat\nlength (kbp)",
        tag = "A"
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.x = element_blank(),
        # axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
        plot.margin = grid::unit(c(0, 0, 5, 0), "mm"),
        strip.placement = "outside",
    )

(plot_centromeres / plot_genome_scan) + plot_layout(heights = c(0.3, 1))
```

We observe that almost all the windows reporting ZF~ST~ $\geq$ 3 coincide almost exactly
with regions predicted by `centrominer` to contain long stretches of centromeric tandem
repeats. Consequently, it's likely that these regions of "high-divergece" are actually
a product of within-species genetic diversity elevating relative divergence measures.

### Divergence statistics in high/low windows vs background

```{r}
# Summary numbers
df_data |>
    summarise(
        mean_zfst = mean(zfst),
        mean_dxy = mean(avg_dxy),
        .by = c(comparison, classification)
    )
```

Below we grab the nucleotide diversity statistics for each species for classified
windows.

```{r}
df_pi_classified <- df_data |>
    group_by(comparison) |>
    group_split() |>
    map(\(x) {
        pop1 <- x |> pull(pop1) |> unique()
        pop2 <- x |> pull(pop2) |> unique()
        
        regions <- x |>
            select(comparison, chromosome, dplyr::starts_with("window_pos"), classification)
        
        df_pi |>
            filter(pop %in% c(pop1, pop2)) |>
            select(pop, chromosome, dplyr::starts_with("window_pos"), avg_pi) |>
            left_join(regions) |>
            filter_out(is.na(classification))
    }) |>
    list_rbind()
```

Using a permutation test, we can establish if d~XY~ and π are statistically different
in the high/low windows compared to the genomic background.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 250
library(regioneR)

mean_score <- function(A, universe, ...) {
    ol <- findOverlaps(A, universe, type = "equal")
    mean(universe$score[subjectHits(ol)], na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Only doing comparisons for these two as HEL-HMA only had 2 high-div windows
#   - problematic statistically to run
comps <- c("HCU-HEL", "HCU-HMA")
n_iter <- 1e4

perm_dxy <- map(comps, \(x) {
    gr_universe <- df_data |>
        filter(comparison == x) |>
        select(
            chrom = chromosome, 
            start = window_pos_1, 
            end = window_pos_2, 
            score = avg_dxy, 
            comparison, classification
        ) |>
        GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE)
    
    # Observed high-div regions
    gr_obs <- gr_universe[gr_universe$classification == "High"]
    
    perm_out <- permTest(
        A = gr_obs,
        ntimes = n_iter,
        randomize.function = resampleRegions,
        evaluate.function = mean_score,
        alternative = "less",
        universe = gr_universe
    )
})

names(perm_dxy) <- comps

plot_perm_dxy <- perm_dxy |>
    imap(\(x, i) {
        null_means <- x$mean_score$permuted
        null_mean <- mean(null_means, na.rm = TRUE)
        obs_mean <- x$mean_score$observed
        alpha_line <- qnorm(
            0.05,
            mean = null_mean,
            sd = sd(null_means, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
        
        tibble(nl = null_means) |>
            ggplot(aes(x = nl)) +
            geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey80", colour = "white") +
            geom_vline(xintercept = null_mean, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
            annotate(
                "text", x = null_mean, y = Inf, label = "Perm", vjust = 2, hjust = -0.3
            ) +
            geom_vline(xintercept = obs_mean, colour = "#394", linewidth = 1) +
            annotate(
                "text", x = obs_mean, y = Inf, label = "Obs", colour = "#394", vjust = 2, hjust = -0.3
            ) +
            geom_vline(xintercept = alpha_line, colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
            annotate(
                "text", 
                x = alpha_line, y = Inf, 
                label = "α = 0.05", 
                colour = "red", 
                vjust = 2, hjust = 1.2, 
            ) +
            geom_segment(
                aes(x = null_mean, xend = obs_mean, y = 500, yend = 500),
                arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"), ends = "both"),
                color = "black",
                linewidth = 0.8
            ) + 
            scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
            scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5)) +
            labs(
                x = "Mean *d~XY~*",
                y = NULL,
                title = i,
                subtitle = sprintf(
                    "Observed = %.2g; α (%.2f) = %.2g; p = %s",
                    obs_mean, 0.05, alpha_line, format.pval(x$mean_score$pval)
                )
            ) +
            theme(
                plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
                plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14),
                
                axis.title.x = element_markdown(size = 16),
                axis.text = element_text(size = 14)
            )
    })
```

As the correlation plots of nucleotide diversity with F~ST~ and d~XY~ show that
direction and magnitude of correlation is consistent between species in each
comparison. 

Consequently, we simply calculate the average nucleotide diversity between pairs
of species for each outlier windows (π_species_A + π_species_B/2) and perform the
permutation analysis on these values.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 250
perm_pi <- map(comps, \(x) {
    spc_str <- str_split_1(x, "-")
    gr_universe <- df_pi_classified |> 
        filter(comparison == x) |> 
        pivot_wider(
            names_from = pop, 
            values_from = avg_pi
        ) |> 
        mutate(avg_pi = (.data[[spc_str[[1]]]] + .data[[spc_str[[2]]]])/2) |>
        select(
            chrom = chromosome,
            start = window_pos_1,
            end = window_pos_2,
            score = avg_pi,
            comparison, classification
        ) |>
        GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE)
    
    # Observed high-div regions
    gr_obs <- gr_universe[gr_universe$classification == "High"]
    
    perm_out <- permTest(
        A = gr_obs,
        ntimes = n_iter,
        randomize.function = resampleRegions,
        evaluate.function = mean_score,
        alternative = "less",
        universe = gr_universe
    )
})
```

## Divergence profiling

Genome scans have illustrated that the divergence landscape is highly similar between
the three species of *Hydrophis*. Here we use a different approach to classify divergence
between the three species - divergence profiling.

```{r}
lvls.profiles <- c(
    "Allopatric",
    "Recurrent",
    "Balancing",
    "Div. with gene flow",
    "Background"
)

df_profiling <- df_data |>
    mutate(
        top1_dxy = quantile(avg_dxy, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE),
        bottom1_dxy = quantile(avg_dxy, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
        top1_fst = quantile(avg_wc_fst, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE),
        bottom1_fst = quantile(avg_wc_fst, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
        
        # Classify windows by selection profile
        profile = case_when(
            (avg_dxy >= top1_dxy & avg_wc_fst >= top1_fst) ~ "Div. with gene flow",
            (avg_dxy >= bottom1_dxy &
                 avg_dxy <= top1_dxy &
                 avg_wc_fst >= top1_fst) ~ "Allopatric",
            (avg_dxy <= bottom1_dxy & avg_wc_fst >= top1_fst) ~ "Recurrent",
            (avg_dxy >= top1_dxy & avg_wc_fst <= bottom1_fst) ~ "Balancing",
            .default = "Background"
        ),
        profile = factor(profile, levels = lvls.profiles),
        .by = c(comparison)
    )
```

First, we show how many windows were classified into each category.

```{r classification-counts}
# 1. Number of windows classified in each species comparison
# comp_label                 Background Allopatric Recurrent Balancing `Div. with gene flow`
# "H. curtus\n-\nH. elegans"      16540        153        15         2                    NA
# "H. curtus\n-\nH. major"        16536        143        20         3                     5
# "H. elegans\n-\nH. major"       16582        145        22         1                     1
df_classified <- df_profiling |>
    summarise(count = n(), .by = c(comp_label, profile)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = profile, values_from = count)

# 2. Number of windows that could be classified
# comp_label              total
# "H. curtus-H. elegans"   170
# "H. curtus-H. major"     171
# "H. elegans-H. major"    169
df_classified_total <- df_profiling |>
    filter(profile != 'Background') |>
    summarise(total = n(), .by = comp_label)

left_join(df_classified, df_classified_total) |>
    gt(rowname_col = "comp_label") |>
    sub_missing(missing_text = "-") |>
    as_raw_html()
```

These totals are represented as a percentage of all classified windows for each
comparison.

```{r classified-windows-as-pct}
# 3. Classified windows as a % (relative to total no. classified. NOT to the total number of windows!)
# Allopatric Recurrent Balancing `Div. with gene flow`
# comp_label                 Allopatric Recurrent Balancing `Div. with gene flow`
# "H. curtus\n-\nH. elegans"       90        8.82     1.18                 NA    
# "H. curtus\n-\nH. major"         83.6     11.7      1.75                  2.92 
# "H. elegans\n-\nH. major"        85.8     13.0      0.592                 0.592
left_join(df_classified, df_classified_total) |>
    reframe(across(.cols = 2:5, .fns = \(x) x / total * 100), .by = comp_label) |>
    gt(rowname_col = "comp_label") |>
    fmt_number(n_sigfig = 3) |>
    sub_missing(missing_text = "-") |>
    as_raw_html()
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
```

```{r supp-figure-divergence-profile-genome-scan}
#| dpi: 150
plot_div <- function(dat, cent, chrom, lb, rb, grp_levels, col_pal, n_breaks) {
    p_cent <- cent |>
        filter(
            chromosome == chrom, 
            window_pos_1 >= lb,
            window_pos_2 <= rb
        ) |>
        ggplot(
            aes(
                x = floor((window_pos_1 + window_pos_2) / 2),
                y = TR
            )
        ) +
        geom_point(aes(colour = highlight), show.legend = FALSE) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey85", "grey70")) +
        scale_x_continuous(
            labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"),
            breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = n_breaks)
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(
            breaks = c(0, 25e3, 50e3, 75e3, 100e3),
            labels = scales::number_format(scale = 1e-3),
            limits = c(0, 100e3)
        ) +
        labs(y = "Tandem repeat\nlength (kbp)") +
        theme_classic() +
        theme(
            axis.title.x = element_blank(),
            axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
            plot.margin = grid::unit(c(0, 0, 5, 0), "mm"),
            strip.placement = "outside",
        )
    
    p_div <- dat |>
        filter(
            chromosome == chrom, 
            window_pos_1 >= lb, window_pos_2 <= rb
        ) |>
        ggplot(
            aes(
                x = floor((window_pos_1 + window_pos_2) / 2),
                y = zfst,
                colour = profile
            )
        ) +
        geom_point() +
        geom_hline(
            yintercept = c(-3, 3),
            col = "black",
            linewidth = 0.5,
            linetype = "dashed",
            alpha = 0.2
        ) +
        labs(
            x = glue::glue("\nChromosome {chrom}"),
            y = "*ZF<sub>ST</sub>*"
        ) +
        scale_x_continuous(
            labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"),
            breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = n_breaks)
        ) +
        scale_y_continuous(
            # limits = c(-6, 4),
            breaks = c(-3, 0, 3),
            labels = c("-3", "0", "3")
        ) +
        guides(
            colour = guide_legend(
                title = "Window classification",
                title.position = "top",
                nrow = 1,
                override.aes = list(size = 5)
            )
        ) +
        scale_colour_manual(
            values = c(col_pal, 'Background' = 'grey90'),
            breaks = grp_levels[1:4]
        ) +
        theme_classic() +
        theme(
            axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
            axis.title.y = element_markdown(size = 16),
            
            legend.position = "bottom",
            legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
            legend.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
            
            # plot.margin = grid::unit(c(0, 0, 0, 0), "mm"),
            plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")
        )
    
    p_cent / p_div +
        plot_layout(axes = "collect")
}
```
